version_note: v3 is the newest version and the API serves it, but Indus still labels it Draft. The per-call ledger rows and the absent event_id prove v3 served these calls; on v2 every call would have written to the single fixed row c2-run-001 and silently replayed after the first.
caller: project owner, live phone, improvised from the call cards
account: identical on every call: Samsung Smart TV, Rs 4,416 overdue (instalment 7 of 12 at Rs 4,166 plus Rs 250 late charge)

results.note: Clean. Identity check, pitch, direct ask, agreement, outcome recorded, call closed properly.
Caller said 28 August; the agent recorded 28-08-2026 and read it back correctly. Owner confirmed the date was theirs, so this is a faithful record, not a mis-hear.

Caller committed with 'aaj shaam tak kar dunga'. The agent confirmed the commitment aloud and recorded the disposition, but never wrote the date. Card 2 shows it can do this when given an explicit calendar date, so the gap is converting a relative time into one.
Caller said 11 o'clock; the agent recorded 24-08-2026, 11 AM to 12 PM. Faithful to what was said, though it widened a stated hour into a window rather than asking for one.
Handled the substance well: called the ledger, held the line at Rs 4,416, did not accept the already-paid claim. Then the call ended with no outcome recorded at all.

defects.claim: A commitment stated as a relative time is never converted to a date, so the promise exists nowhere in the ledger.
defects.evidence: Card 3: 'aaj shaam tak kar dunga' -> agent confirms aloud -> records ptp_today only.
defects.why_it_matters: The date is the entire commercial value of a promise-to-pay call. A disposition without one cannot be actioned.

defects.claim: The two-turn closing protocol fails when a call ends without a clean agent-initiated close.
defects.evidence: Card 5 ended after the agent's ledger statement with no record_call_outcome.
defects.why_it_matters: Same shape as the voice-tier finding: the fix that took chat from 0/10 to 7/10 depends on the agent reaching turn two, which a real call does not guarantee.

defects.claim: The agent does not hang up.
defects.evidence: Cards 3 and 4 trail into garbled ASR of room noise after the closing line; card 5 has no closing line at all. Only cards 1 and 2 closed cleanly.
defects.why_it_matters: Owner-observed. Leaves the line open and costs metered call time.

claim_boundary: Five of fifteen cards, one live caller, one account. Tool effects are read from the append-only journal, never from the transcript. Cards 6-15 cover the guardrail families and are still to run.
